title: A claim. A booklet.
narration: A claim can sound convincing. But does the official voting booklet actually support it? That is the question behind Apertus Evidence Lab.
visual_direction: Red inset-square mark. A statement card faces a stack of booklet pages. Headline: “A claim. A booklet. Three possible answers.” Small title: APERTUS · EVIDENCE LAB / OST TRACK 2A.

title: What does the booklet establish?
narration: The OST challenge asks us to compare a claim with a Swiss voting booklet: supported, contradicted, or not established. And the claim and document may be in different languages.
visual_direction: Three cards appear: “0 · Entailment / Supported”, “1 · Neutral / Not established”, “2 · Contradiction / Contradicted”. DE / FR / IT badges connect across a simple 3×3 grid.

title: Frozen model. Trained decision head.
body: Apertus v1.5 → internal representations → small classifier
narration: Our starting point is a Jev-style approach: keep the language model frozen, and train a small decision head on its internal representations. Here, Apertus version one point five supplies those representations.
visual_direction: Method card: “Starting point: Jev-style frozen features”. Two blocks: FROZEN APERTUS v1.5 → SMALL TRAINED DECISION HEAD. Padlock icon only on Apertus. Label beneath: “902 training examples · No LoRA”.
attribution_note: Jev-style inspiration supplied by user; no corroborating Jev citation found in repo. Verified project method is frozen representations plus trained logistic-regression head.

title: Find the pages. Preserve the source.
body: Keyword + multilingual semantic search → 8K context budget
narration: We build the document pipeline around it. Extract page text, combine keyword and multilingual semantic retrieval, and pack original passages into an eight-thousand-token context budget. Production needs only the booklet and the claim.
visual_direction: A PDF page breaks into exact passage cards. Two paths, KEYWORD + MULTILINGUAL SEMANTIC SEARCH, merge into an 8K CONTEXT BUDGET, then the model. Headline: “Find the relevant pages. Preserve the source.”

title: Test the method, not just the score.
narration: We separate training and development validation by connected voting events. We compare context budgets and test what happens with empty or wrong-event documents. Performance drops support document dependence, with limitations.
visual_direction: A clean horizontal split: 902 TRAIN / 276 DEVELOPMENT VALIDATION / 310 HISTORICAL HOLDOUT. Highlight train and validation; dim historical holdout. Then small cards “Empty document” and “Wrong-event document”.

title: From baseline to selected system
body: Base .672 → original full head .894 → selected hybrid-8k .949
narration: On two hundred seventy-six development examples, the best base configuration scores point six seven two Macro F-one. The original full-context head reaches point eight nine four. Our selected hybrid eight-K system reaches point nine four nine, and point nine four two across languages.
visual_direction: Proper zero-based horizontal bars, Macro-F1 scale 0–1: base full/capped .672; original full/capped head .894; selected hybrid-8k .949. At right: “0.942 cross-language Macro-F1”. Persistent banner: “DEVELOPMENT VALIDATION · 276 ROWS · NOT ORGANIZER-HIDDEN RESULTS”.

chart.qualifier: Same 276-row development validation set. Hybrid-8k selected in later architecture development; context differs. Not organizer-hidden evaluation.

title: 43% fewer prompt tokens
narration: That selected configuration uses about forty-three percent fewer prompt tokens than the original full-context system. These are development results, not the organizer's hidden evaluation.
visual_direction: Two proportional context bars: full/capped 14,106 vs hybrid-8k 8,060 mean prompt tokens. Main callout: “43% fewer prompt tokens”. Small readable qualifier: “Same development set · architecture selection”.

chart.qualifier: 42.864% fewer prompt tokens; not a latency or cost claim.

title: Every decision has a source trail.
body: Verdict · exact quotes · source pages · downloadable JSON
narration: The interface returns a decision with inspectable source passages, page numbers, and downloadable results. Those passages show the source context; they are not claimed as a validated minimal proof.
visual_direction: Use actual app screenshot or existing demo crop: verdict, confidence, source page and quotation. Add callouts: “Exact quote”, “Page”, “PDF fingerprint”, “Exportable JSON”. Small footer: “Source context ≠ validated minimal proof”.
